findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot sort or cursor datetime audit rows
findings.body: When optimized_pagination=true, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime". That class implements get_item_key/value_from_cursor like the integer Paginator: it math.floor/math.ceil's the raw field and feeds the cursor number straight back into the SQL comparison. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page that has rows raises TypeError inside get_item_key while building the next/prev cursor, and a later page would compare a numeric cursor value to a timestamp column. DateTimePaginator already exists for this endpoint and converts timestamps correctly; this path does not, so the new admin pagination option 500s instead of paging audit logs.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are sliced and Django rejects them
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set (the audit-log endpoint always passes True), slices the queryset with a negative start if cursor.offset < 0. Django QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported for any negative start or stop; it does not emit a reverse OFFSET/LIMIT or "handle boundary conditions." Cursor.from_string already accepts a negative offset integer, so an otherwise authorized optimized_pagination request with a crafted or generated cursor 500s. The comment that this is safe because permissions are checked on the queryset is also wrong: the slice never runs, and a negative index would not be an authorization boundary anyway.

findings.title: BasePaginator now silently clamps negative forward offsets for every endpoint
findings.body: The shared BasePaginator.get_result path (used by Paginator and DateTimePaginator across the API, not only audit logs) now sets start_offset = max(0, offset) whenever the cursor is not a previous-page cursor, then slices from there. A forward cursor whose offset is negative used to fail closed on the queryset slice; it now returns the first page and still builds Link cursors as if that page were valid. Previous-page cursors still pass a negative offset through unchanged, so the same negative-index ValueError remains on is_prev. This is not a performance optimization and changes pagination failure behavior globally with no tests.
